messages.subject: googleVis selection input binding example
parts:
Hi,
I am struggling to modify the renderGvis example (from the googleVis package), to include an input binding that sends a selection back to R when something is selected in the scatter plot.  

Would it be possible to get an example of how to do this?  It would save me a lot of fuzzing time.

Thanks,
Brian

messages.author: 726815e70c374c3d
messages.subject: Re: googleVis selection input binding example
parts:
I've been able to get this working using a visible textbox.  Below are the steps I followed.  I experimented with hiding the textbox using tags$head(tags$style(type='text/css', "#selected{ display: none; }")), but then shiny does not recognize the textbox.  If you find a way to accomplish this without displaying the textbox (maybe using a hidden input), please share.
  • Add a textbox input to ui.R: textInput("selected", "Selected", value="")
  • Add a listener to the gvis function in server.R (documented in the googleVis FAQ):
      jscode <- "var sel = chart.getSelection();
               var row = sel[0].row;
               var text = data.getValue(row, 0);               
               $('input#selected').val(text);
               $('input#selected').trigger('change');"
      gvisComboChart(datasetChart(), xvar="date", yvar=c("a", "b"),
                options=list(legend="{position: 'none'}",
                        seriesType="lines",
                        series='{1: {type:"scatter"}}',
                        gvis.listener.jscode=jscode))
  •  Use the selected value in a reactive function in server.R:
selectedData <- renderText({ 
   paste("Selected:", input$selected)
})

messages.subject: Re: googleVis selection input binding example
parts:
I may have stumbled upon a way to hide the input.  The following steps appear to work:
  • Add the following to sidebarPanel in ui.R: tags$head(tags$style(type='text/css', "#selected{ display: none; }"))
  • Replace the textInput call in ui.R with uiOutput("selectedOut"), and add the following to server.R:
output$selectedOut <- renderUI({
textInput("selected", "Selected", value="")

})
outputOptions(output, "selectedOut", suspendWhenHidden=FALSE) 
   
The outputOptions call appears to do the trick.  If you find a more elegant option, please pass it along.
